description: CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became. LS-DATE='2022-07-19' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-YY' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. This program opens no file and is reached by no JCL, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and takes no job parameter - its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 and the group move at L122, never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible here. Arm 7 by a second route: the YEAR role is declared TWICE, once as YYYY and once as YY. Every character is a legitimate token, so a parser that only rejected unknown letters would accept this and then silently prefer one of the two years. It also proves tokens are matched greedily and longest-first, since a parser that read YYYY as two YY fields would reject case01.
